Box 53370Bellevue, Washington 98015-3370RE:  Clarification of HQ 959420, dated August 6, 1996Dear Mr. Killea:     This is in regard to Headquarters Ruling Letter (HQ) 959420issued to you from this office on August 6, 1996.  In HQ 959420Customs determined the country of origin of a fitted sheetpursuant to Section 102.21, Customs Regulations (19 CFR 102.21). Upon further review, Customs has determined that the rationalestated in HQ 959420 should be clarified.     The manufacturing operations performed in Taiwan includedthe weaving, dyeing and printing of the fabric.  In China orThailand, the fabric was cut, sewn and packed for export.Although HQ 959420 correctly determined that the country oforigin of the sheet was conferred by the fabric making process,as per section 102.21(c)(2), it failed to state the correctcountry which conferred origin.   China or Thailand were statedto be the countries in which the fabric-making process occurred. This was an error on our part.  As clearly indicated in thestatement of facts detailing the manufacturing operations, thefabric-making process for the sheet occurs in Taiwan. Accordingly, the country of origin of the sheet is the singlecountry where the fabric making process occurs, that is Taiwan.                              Sincerely,                              John Durant, Director                              Tariff Classification AppealsDivision
